bindings.title: What is on which light
bindings.intro: A binding is one printer, one light, and one segment of it. A change here applies at once, in the running module.
bindings.segment_rule: A segment carries one printer. Two bindings cannot share one, so a segment already in use is offered greyed out with the printer that has it. One printer may sit on several lights — that is what multi-room status is — at the cost of a second steady stream.
bindings.not_saved: Every change here is written into the module's own configuration store, so it survives a restart and an upgrade. A module purge or a fresh install loses it, so keep a copy of a list you want to keep.
bindings.dialog_intro: The segment list is the light's own — read from the controller as you open this — so a segment the light does not have cannot be chosen. A brightness is only written when the whole light is taken, because the rest of a borrowed strip belongs to its owner.
bindings.brightness_note: written once at start, 0 to 255; empty means the module's own default of 128
bindings.brightness_borrowed: none — a borrowed zone never gets a brightness
bindings.segments_from_light: read from the light itself, never typed
bindings.segments_unreadable: The segments of this light could not be read, so there is nothing to pick from: {why}
bindings.segments_unread_line: its segments could not be read: {why}
bindings.printer_gone: A printer the host no longer holds
bindings.printer_missing: this printer is no longer in Prusa Connect
bindings.zone_handed_back: paused — its zone handed back to its owner
bindings.light_off: paused — the light is switched off
bindings.saved: Saved — the module is running on the new set.
bindings.removed: Removed — that segment is free again.
bindings.load_failed: The bindings could not be read
bindings.lights_failed: The lights could not be read
bindings.empty_body: Add a binding and the light appears here, with the segments it reports of itself.
bindings.no_printer_here: No printer on this light. Its segments are all free.
bindings.write_unread: could not read when it last wrote — {why}
bindings.write_no_frame: the module has drawn no picture for this binding yet
bindings.whole_taken: every segment taken by {printer} — 0 of {total} free
bindings.discovered_heading: Lights found, no printer on them
bindings.discovered_note: This list is empty because nothing in this build sweeps your network for lights. A light becomes known to this module when a binding names its address, so a light it has never been told about cannot appear here.
bindings.discovered_how: The way to add one today is the panel above: name the light's address as a new one, and it appears as its own card with the segments it reports.
bindings.unbound_count: {count, plural, one {# without a light} other {# without a light}}
bindings.unbound_empty: Every printer Prusa Connect holds is on a light.
bindings.unbound_note: Every printer Prusa Connect knows about, less the ones already on a light. The button opens the panel with that printer chosen and a light that still has room preselected.
bindings.printer_offline: the host holds no session for it
bindings.no_light_with_room: There is no light with a free segment: take a binding off one first, or name another light's address.
bindings.refused_second: A second binding on a segment already used
bindings.refused_second_why: refused at start, naming both bindings
bindings.refused_brightness: A brightness on a borrowed segment
bindings.refused_brightness_why: never written — it is somebody else's zone
bindings.refused_segment: A segment the light does not have
bindings.refused_segment_why: refused; the list comes from the light, not from us
bindings.refused_light: A light that does not answer
bindings.refused_light_why: its segments cannot be read, so no segment can be picked on it
bindings.no_test: There is no test per binding. The module's preview routes paint a whole light with a diagnostic picture, so a test belongs on a light rather than on one printer's row, and it lives on the Lights screen.
events.title: What each moment shows
events.intro: A moment is a transition — a print finishing, a pause, an error — shown for a length and then given back. One light at a time, because the list of moments belongs to the light.
events.load_failed: The moments could not be read
events.no_lights: No light is bound yet, so there is no moment table to show. Put a printer on a light in Bindings, and the light appears here with all eight of its moments.
events.presets_are_theirs: Each moment carries its own setting per printer. Presets are the light’s own — build and tune them in WLED’s own interface, because this page only names one.
events.strip_no_word: This light is a strip: a word needs a second dimension, so it is not offered here, and a moment set to a word shows the moment’s colour instead.
events.shape_unknown: The module has not drawn a frame for this light yet, so it does not know whether it is a panel or a strip. A word is offered; a strip would show the moment’s colour instead.
events.not_kept: This module has no store to keep a change in: {why}
events.each_moment_then_printers: each moment, then a line per printer
events.preset_placeholder: the preset’s name, as WLED spells it
events.pick_preset: pick one of this light’s presets
events.presets_read: {count, plural, one {# preset read from the light} other {# presets read from the light}} — choose one, so the name is one the light can be asked for
events.presets_unnamed_hidden: {count, plural, one {# slot has no name and is not offered} other {# slots have no name and are not offered}} — a moment names a preset by its name
events.presets_none_yet: This light answered and holds no named presets. Build one in WLED’s own interface, then reopen this page: a moment can only name a preset that exists.
events.presets_typed: The light’s presets could not be read ({why}), so the name is typed and stored as written. A light that is unplugged must not stop you editing.
events.preset_not_on_light: {name} — stored, but the light does not list it now
events.word_undrawable: not drawable by this font: {chars} — the module refuses the word and shows the moment’s colour instead
events.word_too_wide: {word} is too wide for a 256 × 64 panel at the module’s scale of five, so the moment’s colour is shown instead
events.reset_done: Reset — that moment is back to its default for that printer.
events.was_default: That moment was already at its default.
events.footnote: A preset takes the whole light for its moment — capture it, run the preset for the length, put it back — and it is refused on a borrowed zone. While a preset runs the progress bar is gone, and that is the trade.
events.for_forever: forever means until its state changes: until it resumes, until it is cleared, until the light answers. A length such as 60s or 5m is accepted too.
events.preset_not_checked: A preset is named by its name, and the list is read from the light when this page opens. The write itself is stored as written and reaches the light on the next event: nothing here is sent to the light, and a name that no longer matches shows as stored rather than disappearing.
events.kept_without_light: A change here is written into the module’s own store, so it survives a restart and an upgrade, and it is kept whether or not the light is answering. Nothing here is sent to the light.
events.unknown_moments: The store holds rows about moments this build does not have, and they are reported rather than deleted: {list}
colours.title: What each state looks like
colours.intro: One row per condition a printer can be in. A state is not a moment: it lasts until something else happens.
colours.note: Every state can carry a word, and the word is yours to edit — which is also how a light is made to speak another language. A word beats the layout while it holds: a light showing a state with a word shows that word, not the bar and digits. It holds forever by default, or for a length you set.
colours.load_failed: The table could not be read
colours.not_kept: This module has no store to keep a change in: {why}
colours.conditions_note: The light unreachable and the printer lost are not words the host reports: this module computes both from its own reading, because a printer it has lost, and one that has gone quiet beside it, have no state to report — and neither must look like a verdict. They are editable here exactly as a state is.
colours.busy_ready_note: BUSY and READY have no row here. The approved screen gives their two places to the light unreachable and the printer lost, and that is this page. The module still holds both states and still paints them; an override already stored for either keeps working, and this page simply does not edit it.
colours.reset_done: Reset — {state} is back to the colour the table gives it, no word, and a hold of forever.
colours.already_default: There was nothing stored for {state}: it was already at its default.
colours.holds_needs_word: A hold belongs to a word: write one to set a length.
colours.not_drawable: not drawable by this font: {chars} — the panel refuses the word and shows the colour instead
colours.too_wide: {word} does not fit a 256 × 64 panel at the module’s scale of five, so the light shows the colour instead
colours.showing_forever: on the light now, and it holds until the state moves
colours.expired_short: not showing — the hold ran out
colours.expired_why: A light is showing this state and the hold ran out, so nothing shows this word now and nothing will until it is written again. Write it again to bring it back.
colours.later_why: No light is showing this state now. The word runs from the moment a light enters the state.
colours.no_word: This state carries no word: it is drawn as the colour alone.
colours.font_note: The font is the limit, not the text: it holds A–Z, 0–9, a space and the marks . - % : / _ — forty-three glyphs. A character outside that set cannot be drawn, so the module refuses the word and shows the colour; write it in capitals and it draws.
colours.kept_note: A change here is written into the module’s own store, and reaches the light on the painter’s next pass. This page sends nothing to the light.
colours.unknown_states: The store holds rows about states this build does not have, and they are reported rather than deleted: {list}
colours.strip_plain: A strip of 48 pixels filled with {colour}; a strip cannot carry a word
layout.title: How each light is laid out
layout.intro: A panel composes a picture — a bar in its band, the percentage, the job's name. A strip fills, and that is all a strip can do. One layout per binding, so a panel and a strip never share one.
layout.bindings_note: One card at a time: pick the binding to lay out. A warning marks a binding whose arrangement would not fit its panel.
layout.per_binding: A layout belongs to the binding, not to the light: the same printer on a panel and on a strip carries two of them, and two bindings on one light may be laid out differently. Everything here is written into the module's own store and reaches the light on the painter's next pass.
layout.load_failed: The layouts could not be read
layout.no_lights: No light is bound yet, so there is nothing to lay out. Put a printer on a light in Bindings and it appears here, with its own shape.
layout.no_bindings: That light carries no binding, so there is no layout to show.
layout.not_kept: This module has no store to keep a change in: {why}
layout.unknown_layouts: The store holds layouts for bindings this module does not drive, and they are reported rather than deleted: {list}
layout.shape_unknown: The module has not drawn a frame for this binding yet, so it does not know whether the light is a panel or a strip. A layout can be written either way — it is judged when the picture is drawn — but this screen will not offer a composer it cannot place.
layout.bar_rows_note: 1 to 48 rows of the panel. The rest is the text's.
layout.name: Job name
layout.group_content_what: the bar, the percentage and the job's name
layout.group_share_what: take turns, or both at once
layout.lines_count: {on} of 7 on, taking {rows} rows of the text band
layout.lines_note: Each line is seven rows tall, with one blank row between it and the next, and they are taken out of the rows the bar leaves — the picture's own row gets what is left. So the more you switch on, the less room the digits have, and a set that does not fit is refused rather than cropped.
layout.lines_refused: This set does not fit: the lines take {rows} rows and the band has {left}, so there is no room for {missed}. Nothing would be drawn — the module refuses the picture rather than cropping it.
layout.line_remaining_what: 42M — how long the printer says the job has left
layout.line_ends_what: ENDS 11:12 — the time remaining read against the clock, in the zone the timezone setting names
layout.line_temperatures_what: NOZ 221/220 BED 60 — the nozzle at its temperature and its target, and the bed
layout.line_elapsed: How long it has been printing
layout.line_elapsed_what: 1H12M — how long the printer says the job has been running
layout.line_material_what: PLA — the filament's short name, as the printer reported it
layout.line_printer_name_what: HERMES MK4 — the machine's own name, so a light carrying two printers says which one it is showing
layout.line_layer: How far up it has printed
layout.line_layer_what: Z 8.6MM — the nozzle's height. There is no layer count to draw: this machine reports a position and no number of layers, so the line says Z.
layout.line_ends_no_zone: The time it ends at needs the timezone setting. With no zone this module draws no clock at all, so this line stays blank rather than showing the container's own time.
layout.reset_done: Reset — this binding is back to the built-in arrangement, and every value says default again.
layout.already_default: There was nothing stored for this binding: it was already at the built-in arrangement.
layout.not_saved: Not saved — {why} Nothing was written, so the arrangement in force is still the one the controls showed before this change.
layout.saved: Saved. The painter picks it up on its next pass.
layout.rows_out_of_range: A bar takes 1 to 48 rows of a 64-row panel, and that number is outside them. Nothing was written.
layout.seconds_out_of_range: A rotation of no seconds is not a rotation: write a whole number of seconds. Nothing was written.
layout.picture_what: what this binding draws, and whether it fits
layout.fit_band: {height} rows, and a {rows}-row bar leaves {left} for the text
layout.fit_lines_ok: That fits — {band}, and {lines} {verb} {rows} rows of it, leaving {left} for the picture.
layout.fit_lines_over: That does not fit: {lines} are on, and this panel is {height} rows high with a {rows}-row bar, leaving {left} rows for the text. {need} {verb} {needRows} of them, so only {fits} of the {total} lines fit — {held} — and there is no room for {missed}. {rooms} A picture the panel cannot hold is refused rather than cropped, so nothing would be drawn.
layout.fit_what_beside: The digits and the name side by side
layout.room_bar: A bar of {rows} rows or less would take all {count}.
layout.room_bar_off: Switching the bar off would take all {count}.
layout.room_scale: Putting the percentage at scale {scale} would take all {count}.
layout.room_none: Nothing this screen offers makes room for them all: turn one line off.
layout.fit_no_room: That does not fit: a {rows}-row bar on a {height}-row panel covers the panel and leaves nothing for the picture. The module refuses it rather than cropping it, so nothing would be drawn.
layout.fit_no_text: That does not fit: a {rows}-row bar leaves {left} rows and the smallest word this font draws is {glyph} rows. The module refuses the picture rather than cropping it, so this panel would draw nothing until that changes.
layout.fit_scale: That does not fit: {band}, and {digits}. A scale the band cannot hold is refused rather than cropped, so nothing would be drawn.
layout.fit_beside: That does not fit side by side: the digits at scale {scale} are {digits} rows and the name is {name} rows, and the band leaves {left}. The module refuses the picture rather than cropping it.
layout.fit_unknown: The module has not drawn a frame for this binding, so the panel's own height is not known and this screen cannot check the arithmetic. The write is allowed: the module judges the fit when it draws, and refuses rather than crops.
layout.sketch_alt: The layout to scale: a {rows}-row bar on a {height}-row panel
layout.sketch_caption: The boxes are the arithmetic, to scale: the bar's band, the text band, the digits at their scale, the name's room when the two are side by side, and one hatched box per optional line at the bottom. A box taller than its band is the picture that does not fit. These are not the module's glyphs, which only the light itself draws.
layout.picture_alt: The picture this module has drawn for this binding
layout.picture_caption: What the module is drawing now: its own reconstruction from the frame it decided, not a screenshot — this firmware cannot read its pixels back.
layout.picture_no_job: No job is running, so the panel is showing its state colour: the composer's picture is a print in progress, and it needs one.
layout.side_by_side_quiet: Only a job in progress composes. Idle, finished, stopped and error keep the plain state colour, so a layout's look needs a print — that is the rule, not a fault.
layout.side_by_side_what: Side by side draws the digits on the left at a capped scale and the job's name on the right, cut to the room that is left. With fewer than three glyphs of room the name is not drawn at all.
layout.side_by_side_needs_both: Side by side needs both the percentage and the job's name: with one of them off it draws exactly as taking turns does.
layout.strip_what: A strip is one dimension, so this is the whole of it: the module fills the run and writes no bar band, no percentage and no name. That is the hardware, not a missing feature — a word needs a second dimension.
layout.strip_picture_alt: The fill this module is drawing on {light}
layout.strip_fill: It fills from the left: {lit} of {total} pixels carry the completed part of the job, and the rest show the colour of what is not lit.
layout.strip_zero: At 0 % nothing is lit and the whole run shows the unlit colour.
layout.strip_full: At 100 % the whole run is the printing green.
layout.strip_brightness: Brightness {level}, from the binding. A brightness is written only when the whole strip is taken, and it is set in Bindings.
layout.strip_brightness_borrowed: This binding drives {segment}, not the whole strip, so no brightness is written: the rest of the run belongs to its owner.
layout.strip_fill_note: What 0 % and 100 % do is the fill behaviour, which the requirements make editable and this build has no route for: the lines above are what the module does today, not settings.
layout.strip_row_yours: This binding has a layout of its own, stored and kept: the module composes only a panel, so it changes nothing on a strip. Reset clears it.
layout.note_store: Every change is written into the module's own store, so it survives a restart and an upgrade, and a module purge or a fresh install loses it.
layout.note_reset: A binding nobody has laid out answers the built-in default rather than an empty box, and every value says whether it is yours or the default. There is one reset per binding because the route resets the whole row.
devices.title: Lights
devices.intro: One card per light: what the hardware is, its own segments, its own presets, the tests that prove the pixels and the copies this module keeps. A light is on this page whether or not a printer is shown on it — which printer sits on which light is Bindings' business, not this page's.
devices.discovery_note: Finding lights on the network needs mDNS from your LAN to reach this container: the host has to pass that traffic across its Docker bridge (docs/mdns-in-docker.md). This module does not browse for them yet, so typing a light's address is the way today.
devices.add_label: Add a light by its address
devices.add_hint: The light is read before it is added. Nothing is kept unless a light answers at that address.
devices.added: {address} answered and is on the list. It calls itself {called}, runs firmware {firmware}, drives {pixels} pixels and is a {shape}.
devices.added_unnamed: nothing yet — it reports no name
devices.load_failed: The lights could not be read
devices.no_lights: No lights here yet. Type a light's address above and it will be read and added — no printer has to be free, and nothing else needs setting up first.
devices.unbound_note: A light no printer is shown on yet. It is first here, so a light you have just added is the first thing you see and the thing you can act on.
devices.unbound_none: Every light here has a printer on it.
devices.bound_heading: Lights with a printer on them
devices.bound_none: No light here has a printer on it yet.
devices.open_named: {name} — open this light's own interface in a new window
devices.open_address: {address} — open this light's own interface in a new window
devices.no_name_yet: has not answered yet, so it has no name
devices.not_answering_why: This light did not answer: {why} Its tests and its restore are off, because a button that cannot reach the light is a button that always fails.
devices.facts_source: The name the light calls itself, its firmware, its pixel count and its shape are the light's own answer: this module reads them when the light is added, and again whenever a snapshot is taken. The segments below are read from the light each time this page is opened.
devices.segments_read_only: read from the light — edit them in WLED
devices.segments_unread: The segments could not be read: {why}
devices.presets_read_only: Read-only, and deliberately: presets are built and tuned in WLED's own interface. This page names one and never carries or edits its body.
devices.presets_unread: The list is empty because the light could not be read, not because it holds none: {why}
devices.presets_not_served: This build does not serve the presets route, so the light's own table cannot be read here: {why}
devices.presets_none: This light answered and holds no presets of its own.
devices.tests_need_printer: These tests paint a light this module is drawing on, so they need a printer on it: add one in Bindings and they work here.
devices.remove_bound: {count, plural, one {a binding still writes to it — remove that first} other {# bindings still write to it — remove those first}}
devices.remove_note: Nothing is written to this light, so it can come off the list. Any snapshots already taken stay in the module's data directory.
devices.tests_before: Each of these paints the light itself, for {hold} seconds, and then the module's own picture comes back. Nothing here runs on its own — each one is a press.
devices.identify_no_route: identify — the light on and off, one second each way, five times — has a route on this build, but this button is not wired to it yet, so it is off rather than offering one that always fails.
devices.tests_disabled: The light is not answering, so its tests are off.
devices.test_fired: {pattern} is on the light for {hold} seconds. {what}
devices.test_fired_word: {word} is on the light for {hold} seconds.
devices.snapshots_when: This build takes a snapshot when you press the button, and on no timer: a snapshot exists because a dead light cannot be read, so the copy that matters is the one taken while the light was alive. Each one is a file in the module's own data directory.
devices.snapshots_none: No snapshot yet. Take one before you change anything on the light.
devices.snapshots_unreadable: The snapshot folder could not be read: {why}
devices.snapshots_no_folder: This module was granted no data directory, so no snapshot can be taken or kept: {why}
devices.snapshot_not_clone: Not a clone — it cannot give back {members}. No configuration dump on these lights carries the wifi password, so a restored light keeps the network it is on.
devices.snapshot_detail_failed: That snapshot could not be read: {why}
devices.restore_nw: The network section is written whole except for {members}, because a configuration write that leaves it out clears the light's linked remote.
devices.restore_unrestorable: This file cannot be turned into a restore: {why}
devices.restore_warning_destructive: This rewrites the light's whole configuration — its LED setup, its defaults, its timers, its access point, its name and its presets — and asks it to reboot. For about fifteen seconds the light is gone, and whatever is on that light now is replaced.
devices.restore_never_fired: Restore has never been run against a real light on this build. Reading a configuration back is not writing one: what the hardware does with this is unproven.
devices.restore_safety: The route takes a snapshot of the light as it stands before it writes anything, and names it in the answer, so a restore that goes wrong can be put back. A light that cannot be copied is not restored at all.
devices.restore_nw_warning: It is not a clone: the wifi credential is never written, and the firmware revision, the hardware revision and the wifi section's own settings are withheld. The light keeps the network it is on.
devices.restore_understand: I understand this rewrites the light and restarts it
devices.restore_now: rewrite the light from this snapshot
devices.restore_done: Restored {id} onto the light, which answered again {seconds} seconds later ({observed}). The safety snapshot {safety} is kept.
devices.restore_observed: it was seen to go away and come back
devices.restore_not_observed: it answered throughout, so no outage was measured
devices.restore_failed: The restore was refused or did not finish: {why}
devices.replace_hint: not built here — a swap would check identical hardware and match segments by name
devices.replace_none: There is no replace route in this build. What it asks for is a gate on the hardware — the same shape and the same pixel count, or no swap — segments matched by name, a poll every 23 seconds while a missing segment is created in WLED, and the old snapshot written onto the new box. None of that can be done through this API, so no button is offered: a button that cannot work teaches you to distrust the ones that do.
devices.replace_bindings: A binding can be pointed at a different light in Bindings. That is not a swap: nothing checks the hardware, nothing matches a segment by name, and nothing restores a snapshot on the new box.
devices.replace_out_of_scope: Physical mounting is out of scope either way: the module cannot know where a replacement is hung, or which way up.
devices.note_split: Bindings says which printer is on which light. This page says what the light is, and names a printer only to say which segment it sits on.
devices.note_segments: Segments and presets belong to WLED, exactly as each other: they are read here and edited there, so a copy on this page cannot drift from the light.
devices.note_presets: The four tests are the instrument, not decoration: this firmware cannot be asked what its pixels are, so a picture on the wall is checked by eye.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.intro: Why the light is doing that. The four tiles and the picture are the present tense — what the module decided and what it wrote — and the list under them is every instant it can still name.
diagnostics.load_failed: The module could not be read
diagnostics.nothing_yet: Nothing has been drawn yet, so there is nothing to diagnose.
diagnostics.now_body_same: This is what the module reports now.
diagnostics.now_body_other: Not happening now: the module reports {situation}. The tiles below are always the live answer, so read this one as what to look at instead.
diagnostics.now_body_none: None of the three is what the module reports now — the tiles below are the live answer, and this is what to look at when the light is {situation}.
diagnostics.read_printing: Read the printer tile and the reason tile together: a connected printer, a reading seconds old, and a reason of progress mean the fill is the printer's own percentage. The last write should say it landed, and nothing here needs you.
diagnostics.read_finished: Read the reading tile and the reason tile together: the age keeps climbing and goes stale, and the reason is not-a-live-job — finished, stopped or idle, so there is nothing to fill. The picture holds its colour anyway, because a job that is over cannot be retracted by silence, and the log has one line for the staleness and nothing after it however long the quiet lasts.
diagnostics.read_lost: Read the last-write tile and the reason tile together. The reason is still progress — the frame is right — and the last write failed: that pair is the whole difference between what the module decided and what reached the light. It retries on a wait that doubles from a second to half a minute, and nothing skips that wait.
diagnostics.reason_unfamiliar: a reason this page does not know — it was written by a newer module than this bundle
diagnostics.transport_state_meaning: port 80 — one request per change of picture, and one repaint a minute on a still one.
diagnostics.transport_pixels_meaning: port 4048 — pixels, pushed once a second for as long as the job runs, because this firmware draws pixels only in realtime.
diagnostics.transport_rule: Which one carries the picture above comes from the module's own rule — a panel holding a job in progress, with a layout that draws something of its own, goes as pixels, and everything else is a JSON state write. The module does not report which transport the last write used.
diagnostics.frame_route: the module's own frame, from GET /frames
diagnostics.frame_alt: The picture this module is drawing on {light}, showing {printer}
diagnostics.frame_missing: this frame could not be drawn
diagnostics.timeline_route: the instants the module reports, in order
diagnostics.timeline_said_nothing: the printer said nothing this build has a reading of
diagnostics.timeline_and_stale: — and nothing since, so the reading is stale
diagnostics.timeline_read: took the reading the picture above is decided from, and decided {reason}
diagnostics.timeline_wrote: wrote the frame to {light} — the controller took it
diagnostics.timeline_write_failed: wrote the frame to {light} — it did not land: {why}
diagnostics.timeline_paused: paused for {length} — no writes and no log lines until it resumes
diagnostics.timeline_empty: The module reports no instant yet: it has not taken a reading.
diagnostics.timeline_limit: Only what this module did. Every line is either something the printer reported that made us act, or something we did to the light — a frame, a failure and its widening retries. Progress is never logged: a printing job is one line where it starts and none during it. Changes made elsewhere on the controller are not followed.
diagnostics.timeline_no_history: That is the whole timeline, and it is this short because the module keeps no history: this build serves no log route, so nothing here can tell you about an earlier write. The module's own lines go to the host's log, and this screen cannot read that. What it can show is the three instants it reports — the printer's last word, the reading the picture is decided from, and the last write with its outcome.
diagnostics.reasons_route: one of these is on every frame
diagnostics.reasons_intro: In the order the module applies its rules, so the first one that matches is the one on the frame — which is why this list also says what is not happening.
diagnostics.reason_disconnected: the host holds no session with this printer, so the last state it reported is a memory rather than an observation — dim red, and never the remembered progress
diagnostics.reason_stale: connected, but silent past the thirty-second horizon, with a last word a later reading could overturn — dim red, and never the remembered progress
diagnostics.reason_unknown_state: the printer said nothing, or a word this build has no reading of — dim blue, because that is not a verdict
diagnostics.reason_not_a_live_job: finished, stopped or idle: nothing on the bed to fill, so the state's own colour alone
diagnostics.reason_progress_unknown: a job is on the bed but its percentage cannot be believed, so the colour and the job's name and no digits
diagnostics.reason_progress: a live job with a percentage this build may present: the fill is the printer's own progress
diagnostics.reason_paused_frozen: a paused print: the fill is the progress it stopped at, frozen there
diagnostics.reason_starting: a job taken but not yet moving: the whole range is the waiting yellow rather than the printing green, because a print at nought per cent must not look like a finished one
diagnostics.limit_strip_word_why: impossible — a strip has no second dimension, so it shows the moment's colour
diagnostics.limit_quiet: A printer that goes quiet mid-job
diagnostics.limit_quiet_why: shown as do not trust this, never as progress
diagnostics.limit_elsewhere: A change made elsewhere on the controller
diagnostics.limit_elsewhere_why: not followed — this is a record of our own actions, not a general audit
diagnostics.limit_pixels_why: cannot be read back on this firmware — a picture is checked by eye
diagnostics.limit_history_why: the module keeps none and serves no route for one; its lines go to the host's log
